Composite/chatef shəva: a combination of the שְׁוָא and one of the three basic vowels, used to give gutturals a bit more sound in place of a plain vocal שְׁוָא. Appendix A 2a lists this sign in the Reduced Short column for the a-class.
Composite/chatef shəva under gutturals; Appendix A 2a lists this sign in the Reduced Short column for the i-class.
Composite/chatef shəva under gutturals; Appendix A 2a lists this sign in the Reduced Short column for the u-class.

shevaRules.rule: The שְׁוָא is vocal (has the 'hurried' a-as-in-above sound, transliterated ə) at the beginning of a word, e.g. שְׁמוֹ [shə-mo].
The שְׁוָא is vocal when it is the second of two consecutive shevas, e.g. the מְ in יִשְׁמְרוּ [yish-mə-ru].
In all other cases, the שְׁוָא is silent, e.g. as under the ד in מִדְבָּר [mid-bar].

Under the guttural consonants, the שְׁוָא is often modified so that it has a bit more sound (e.g. אֲשֶׁר instead of the unmodified *אְשֶׁר). This modified type is called חֲטֶף שְׁוָא (abbreviated as שְׁוָא) and is a combination of the שְׁוָא and one of the three basic vowels (patach, segol, or qamets).

uncertainties: Diacritic marks (macron/breve) over the English pronunciation vowels in the Lesson 3 chatef-shəva chart ('a in Arise', 'e in Excuse', 'o in Omit') could not be confirmed pixel-by-pixel from the scan resolution; recorded without diacritics.

The Lesson 2 vowel chart's merged pronunciation cells (spanning two rows for qamets-he/patach, qamets-chatuf/cholem-vav, and qibbuts/shureq) were read from cell-boundary/shading cues in the scan; exact vertical span of each merge should be re-verified against a cleaner render.

Appendix A section 2a table (pp. a-4/a-5, PDF 144-145) — 'Pure Long / Lengthened Short / Short / Reduced Short' by a-class/i-class/u-class — is partially obscured in the scan by handwritten circles, underlines, and marginal notes overlapping the printed cells; the length classifications assigned to each Lesson-2 vowel entry in this file were inferred from the legible portions (row labels, the explicit a-6 text on qamets-chatuf, and the explicit Reduced-Short listing of the chatef signs) rather than read cell-by-cell with full certainty, and should be re-checked against a clean scan of a-4/a-5.

Length is explicitly stated by the book (Appendix A a-6) to be contextual, not a fixed property of a vowel sign — e.g. the qamets sign can represent either 'lengthened short a-class' or, in a closed unstressed syllable, 'short u-class' (qamets-chatuf). For the four Lesson-2 chart rows that bundle a bare form and a mater-lectionis form under one name (qamets-he, tsere-yod, chireq-yod, cholem-vav), the 'length' field records both possibilities rather than a single value, since the book itself does not collapse them to one.

No separate printed entry or Hebrew name for plain vocal/silent שְׁוָא as a 'vowel' was found in Lesson 2's consolidated vowel chart — the book's own heading treats שְׁוָא (Lesson 3) as distinct from 'The Vowels' (Lesson 2), so it is represented only via shevaRules, not as a vowels[] entry, consistent with how the book presents it.
